description.value: The study compared cortical thickness among AUD patients, HR individuals, and non-HR participants and examined associations between cortical thickness and trait empathy in empathy-related brain regions.

spans.text: the main aim of our study was the investigation of CT differences between patients with AUD and individuals with (HR) and without (non-HR) increased familial risk for developing AUD.

description.value: Observational cross-sectional study of AUD patients, HR individuals, and non-HR participants, with one MRI assessment and no intervention.

spans.text: The study was approved by the local ethics committee and conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki (1964).

spans.text: Results of the contrasts non-HR > AUD and HR > AUD for the left and right hemispheres (AUD patients with alcohol use disorder/HR healthy participants with a familial predisposition for alcoholism/non-HR healthy participants without familial predisposition for alcohol use disorder) ( p < 0.05, FDR corrected)

value: Relative to the HR group, patients with AUD showed reduced cortical thickness in empathy-related frontal and insular regions, including the left inferior and superior frontal gyri, the right precuneus, bilaterally in the middle frontal gyri, and several segments of the insula.

These findings provide preliminary evidence of reduced cortical thickness in empathy-associated brain regions in patients with AUD; cortical thickness did not differ significantly between the HR and non-HR groups.

spans.text: More specifically, relative to HR participants, AUD patients showed decreased CT in the left IFG, the left superior frontal gyrus, and the right precuneus as well as bilaterally in the middle frontal gyri and in several segments of the insula.

value: Compared with the non-HR group, AUD patients showed reduced cortical thickness in the left insula, the right middle frontal gyrus, and bilaterally in the superior frontal gyri and the precuneus.

These results provide preliminary evidence of cortical thickness reduction in empathy-associated brain regions in patients with AUD relative to healthy participants without familial predisposition for AUD.

spans.text: Compared with non-HR participants, CT in the AUD group was decreased in the left insula, the right middle frontal gyrus, and bilaterally in the superior frontal gyrus and in the precuneus.

name.value: perspective taking and CT in the right IFG

definition.value: “perspective taking” scores correlated negatively with CT in the triangular part of the right IFG

spans.text: In the AUD group, “perspective taking” scores correlated negatively with CT in the triangular part of the right IFG ( r = − 0.626; p = 0.022) as well as with the right middle ( r = − 0.584; p = 0.036) and the left superior ( r = − 0.610; p = 0.027) frontal gyri.
relevant regions in the frontal cortex (IFG, superior and middle frontal gyri)

value: In the AUD group, perspective taking scores correlated negatively with cortical thickness in the triangular part of the right inferior frontal gyrus.
The association between higher perspective taking scores and reduced cortical thickness was contrary to expectations and may reflect poorer insight and overestimation of perspective-taking skills.

definition.value: increased “personal distress” scores were related to reduced CT in the orbital part of the left IFG

spans.text: Furthermore, increased “personal distress” scores were related to reduced CT in the orbital part of the left IFG ( r = − 0.596; p = 0.031).
relevant regions in the frontal cortex (IFG, superior and middle frontal gyri)

value: In the AUD group, increased personal distress scores were related to reduced cortical thickness in the orbital part of the left inferior frontal gyrus.
The relationship may reflect detrimental stress-related effects of increased personal distress or impaired inhibition of the self-perspective due to deficient cortical structure.

name.value: fantasy and CT in the insula

definition.value: higher “fantasy” scores correlated with increased CT in the right and left inferior segments of the circular sulcus of the insulae

value: In the AUD group, higher fantasy scores correlated with increased cortical thickness in the right and left inferior segments of the circular sulcus of the insula.
The positive relationship between fantasy scores and higher insular cortical thickness was unexpected, but the affective representation of fictitious characters may plausibly involve the insula.
